html:
The Murui-Muinane are the largest group of the Witoto (Huitoto) peoples of the Amazon, living between the Caquetá and Putumayo rivers in south-eastern Colombia and across the border in Peru.

They lived in great communal houses, the malocas, farming manioc and coca in forest clearings. Around 1900 the rubber company of Julio César Arana, later the British-registered Peruvian Amazon Company, enslaved them to gather rubber. Flogging, torture and killings cut the Witoto population from tens of thousands to a few thousand in the Putumayo genocide. The British consul Roger Casement exposed the atrocities in a report of 1912. During the 1930s many Witoto were moved from Colombia into Peru. Today they live in reserves on both sides of the border.
sum: The Murui-Muinane are the largest group of the Witoto (Huitoto) peoples of the Amazon, living between the Caquetá and Putumayo rivers in south-eastern Colombia and across the border in Peru.
